classification_basis: Implemented entries were reviewed against the official page, fixtures, and both engines. Summaries, analysis classes, and delegation recommendations for unimplemented entries were drafted from the official page and assigned a status by the documented rules in docs/architecture/sei-cert-rule-pack.md; review them against the official page before promoting an entry.

rules.title: Prevent class initialization cycles
rules.summary: Static initialization must not form cycles, within a class or across classes, that let code observe fields before they receive their intended values.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Static initializer depends on another static value that is still uninitialized due to circular init order.
rules.compliant_concept: Static fields are ordered or decoupled so every value is initialized before any read.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags benign static references between classes whose initialization order never actually cycles.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Cycles spanning several classes or files are invisible to single-file pattern matching.

rules.title: Do not reuse public identifiers from the Java Standard Library
rules.summary: Do not name classes, interfaces, variables, or packages after publicly visible identifiers of the Java standard library.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Declaring a type such as Vector or Date in user code that shadows a standard-library name.
rules.compliant_concept: Choosing distinct names that do not collide with JDK public identifiers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: A list of JDK names flags unrelated identifiers in contexts where no confusion arises.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Incomplete JDK name lists miss less common shadowed identifiers.

rules.title: Do not modify the collection's elements during an enhanced for statement
rules.summary: Assigning a new value to an enhanced-for iteration variable never alters the iterated collection or array; code must not rely on such assignment to update elements.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reassigning the enhanced-for loop variable expecting the collection element to change.
rules.compliant_concept: Treat the loop variable as final; update elements through an index or list iterator.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Intentional local reuse of the loop variable for temporary computation gets flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mutation through aliases or nested helper methods is not visible syntactically.

rules.title: Do not sign code that performs only unprivileged operations
rules.summary: Only sign code that genuinely requires elevated privileges; signing unprivileged code needlessly grants it trust and widens attack surface.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Signing a JAR or applet whose operations need no special permissions.
rules.compliant_concept: Leaving unprivileged code unsigned so it runs in the restricted sandbox.

exceptions.summary: Internal-only builds may sign unprivileged code with distinct internal keys, never shipped to production.
Applets may be signed while still running sandboxed with restricted privileges (Java 7u21 or later).

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Signing for integrity in internal pipelines may be legitimate and not privilege-motivated.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether signed code actually needs privileges cannot be seen from source patterns.

rules.title: Place all security-sensitive code in a single JAR and sign and seal it
rules.summary: Security-sensitive and privileged code should be packaged together in one JAR that is both signed and sealed to prevent package injection or mix-and-match attacks.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Privileged code split across unsealed or unsigned JARs, allowing foreign classes into its packages.
rules.compliant_concept: Single signed JAR with Sealed: true in its manifest containing all sensitive code.

exceptions.summary: Fully independent groups of privileged code may live in separate sealed packages or JARs.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Manifest checks may flag non-sensitive libraries that do not need sealing.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Determining which code is security-sensitive needs design knowledge beyond syntax.

rules.title: Do not trust the values of environment variables
rules.summary: Environment variable values can be manipulated by whoever launches the process and must not be trusted for security decisions; prefer reliable sources such as system properties.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using System.getenv values like USER or PATH to authenticate or authorize.
rules.compliant_concept: Deriving identity or configuration from trusted sources and validating any environment input.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags benign getenv use for non-security configuration.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Security decisions reached via flows through helpers or config wrappers are missed.

rules.title: Do not disable bytecode verification
rules.summary: Never turn off JVM bytecode verification, since unverified classes can break type safety and subvert security guarantees.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Launching the JVM with -Xverify:none or -noverify in scripts or manifests.
rules.compliant_concept: Running with default verification enabled for all loaded classes.

exceptions.summary: The primordial class loader may skip bytecode verification for boot class path classes.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Matching flags in test or tooling scripts not used in production.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Flags set through environment variables, wrapper launchers, or deployment config outside the repo are missed.

rules.title: Do not deploy an application that can be remotely monitored
rules.summary: Production Java applications must not expose remote monitoring or debugging interfaces such as JVMTI agents, JPDA, or unauthenticated JMX to untrusted parties.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Starting with jdwp, -agentlib, or unauthenticated remote JMX listening on network interfaces.
rules.compliant_concept: Disable remote debugging/monitoring or restrict it with authentication, TLS, and local-only binding.

exceptions.summary: Remote monitoring is permitted when only programs inside the local trusted network can possibly connect.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Debug options in development launch configurations are flagged despite never being deployed.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Options injected by container images, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, or ops tooling outside source are missed.

rules.title: Production code must not contain debugging entry points
rules.summary: Code shipped to production must not retain debugging back doors, such as main methods or test hooks left in deployed web components.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A main() or debug servlet left in a deployed J2EE application class.
rules.compliant_concept: Debug and test entry points removed or excluded from production builds.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags legitimate main() in CLI tools or classes excluded from the deployed artifact.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Debug endpoints implemented as normal handlers or feature flags look like ordinary code.

rules.title: Do not suppress or ignore checked exceptions
rules.summary: Checked exceptions must be handled meaningfully or propagated; catching and silently ignoring them hides failures and leaves state inconsistent.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Empty catch block or one that only logs and continues as if nothing failed.
rules.compliant_concept: Recover appropriately, rethrow, or wrap and propagate the exception.

exceptions.summary: Exceptions during resource release may be suppressed when the failure cannot affect later behavior.
Code unable to recover at its level may let exceptions propagate to higher-level handlers.
InterruptedException may be swallowed by Thread subclasses or code implementing the interruption policy.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Catch blocks that legitimately ignore close() failures or document intentional suppression get flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Handlers that only print a stack trace and continue look non-empty yet still suppress.

rules.title: Do not allow exceptions to expose sensitive information
rules.summary: Exceptions and their messages or stack traces must not reveal sensitive details such as file paths, configuration, or internal structure to untrusted callers.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Propagating or displaying raw exception messages or traces to users or clients.
rules.compliant_concept: Catch, log internally, and return a generic sanitized error to the caller.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags exception output that only reaches internal logs or trusted administrators.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaks via exception types, timing, or wrapped messages across layers are missed.

rules.title: Prevent exceptions while logging data
rules.summary: Logging must not itself throw exceptions that disrupt processing; use logging mechanisms robust to failure rather than raw console or stream writes.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Logging via a call that can throw, aborting the handler or error path.
rules.compliant_concept: Use a robust logging framework whose failures do not propagate into business logic.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags System.err usage in places where failure would be harmless.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Custom logging wrappers that can throw are indistinguishable by syntax.

rules.title: Restore prior object state on method failure
rules.summary: When a method fails, objects it modified must be returned to a consistent prior state so later operations do not see corrupted data.
rules.noncompliant_concept: State partially updated before an exception leaves the object inconsistent.
rules.compliant_concept: Validate first, use rollback or finally, or mutate only after success.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags benign ordering where partial updates are harmless or immediately discarded.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Corrupting partial updates spanning multiple fields or methods are not syntactically evident.

rules.title: Do not complete abruptly from a finally block
rules.summary: A finally block must not end abruptly via return, break, continue, or throw, because that discards any exception or result from the try.
rules.noncompliant_concept: return, break, continue, or throw statement inside a finally clause.
rules.compliant_concept: finally block that completes normally, only performing cleanup.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: break/continue targeting loops wholly inside the finally block are wrongly flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Calls in finally that may throw unchecked exceptions are not detected.

rules.title: Do not let checked exceptions escape from a finally block
rules.summary: Checked exceptions raised in a finally block must not propagate out of it, since they mask the original exception and skip later cleanup.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling close() or similar throwing method in finally without handling its exception.
rules.compliant_concept: Handle exceptions inside finally or use try-with-resources.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags calls in finally that do not actually declare checked exceptions.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Without types, a pattern cannot tell which finally-block calls throw checked exceptions.

rules.title: Do not throw undeclared checked exceptions
rules.summary: Do not throw checked exceptions that a method does not declare, e.g. via sneaky-throw tricks, Class.newInstance, or bytecode manipulation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using reflection, generics casts, or Thread.stop-style tricks to throw undeclared checked exceptions.
rules.compliant_concept: Declare thrown checked exceptions or wrap them in an unchecked type.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags generic rethrow helpers used correctly with unchecked exceptions.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Many sneaky-throw idioms look like ordinary generic calls.

rules.title: Do not throw RuntimeException, Exception, or Throwable
rules.summary: Methods should not throw the overly general RuntimeException, Exception, or Throwable types, which force callers into catch-all handling.
rules.noncompliant_concept: throw new RuntimeException / Exception / Throwable from application code.
rules.compliant_concept: Throw a specific, well-defined exception type matching the failure.

exceptions.summary: Exception-sanitizing classes may translate specific exceptions into generic ones for security policy.

false_positive_risks: Exception-sanitizing classes permitted by ERR07-J-EX0 are reported for review.
false_negative_risks: Rethrowing a generic exception held in a variable, and generic exceptions created by factory methods, are not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: throw of RuntimeException, Exception, or Throwable, and throws clauses naming Exception or Throwable (main excluded).

rules.title: Do not catch NullPointerException or any of its ancestors
rules.summary: Do not catch NullPointerException or its supertypes to mask null dereferences; prevent nulls with explicit checks instead.
rules.noncompliant_concept: catch (NullPointerException|RuntimeException|Exception|Throwable) used to handle null dereferences.
rules.compliant_concept: Explicit null checks or null objects instead of catching NPE.

exceptions.summary: A catch-all block may process exceptions, such as filtering sensitive data, before rethrowing them.
Worker or event-dispatch threads may catch RuntimeException when running untrusted tasks via abstractions.
Fault-tolerant systems may catch and log broad exceptions like Throwable at suitable abstraction levels.

false_positive_risks: None expected for NullPointerException handlers.
false_negative_risks: Handlers for RuntimeException, Exception, or Throwable used to mask null dereferences are not reported, because ERR08-J-EX0 to EX2 permit common catch-all designs.

implementation.coverage_note: Handlers naming NullPointerException, alone or in a multi-catch union.

rules.title: Do not allow untrusted code to terminate the JVM
rules.summary: Untrusted code must not be able to stop the whole JVM via System.exit or Runtime.exit/halt; such calls should be restricted.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Library or plugin code calling System.exit without a policy preventing it.
rules.compliant_concept: Prevent untrusted exit calls via policy, and signal errors through exceptions instead.

exceptions.summary: Command-line utilities may call System.exit(), for instance on missing required arguments.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags exit calls in genuine command-line main methods.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Exit reached through reflection or indirect wrappers is missed.

rules.title: Do not ignore values returned by methods
rules.summary: Return values that convey status or results, such as from File.delete or immutable String methods, must be checked or used rather than discarded.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling a method whose result signals success or holds the result, then ignoring it.
rules.compliant_concept: Inspect the returned value and act on failure or use the new object.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags discarded results whose value is genuinely irrelevant to the caller.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Unknown project methods with meaningful returns are not in any API list.

rules.title: Do not use a null in a case where an object is required
rules.summary: Do not use a null reference where an object is required, such as dereferencing, unboxing, or passing to methods that reject null.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Dereferencing a value that may be null on some execution path.
rules.compliant_concept: Check for null, use Optional, or guarantee non-null by contract.

exceptions.summary: A method may dereference an unchecked parameter if it documents possibly throwing NullPointerException.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Cannot see guards or contracts ensuring non-null, flagging safe dereferences.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Nulls flowing from other methods, fields, or collections are invisible.

rules.title: Do not use the Object.equals() method to compare two arrays
rules.summary: Arrays must not be compared with Object.equals, which tests identity; use Arrays.equals or Arrays.deepEquals to compare contents.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling equals() on an array reference expecting element-wise comparison.
rules.compliant_concept: Arrays.equals or Arrays.deepEquals for content comparison.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Identity comparison may be intended, yielding false alarms.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Without type information, array-typed receivers are not recognized.

rules.title: Do not use the equality operators when comparing values of boxed primitives
rules.summary: Do not compare boxed primitives such as Integer or Boolean with == or !=, which compares references rather than values.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using == between two Integer, Long, or Boolean objects.
rules.compliant_concept: Use equals(), compare(), or unbox to primitives first.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Comparisons where one side is primitive (auto-unboxed) look identical syntactically.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Boxed variables declared elsewhere or via generics are not recognized.

rules.title: Do not pass arguments to certain Java Collections Framework methods that are a different type than the collection parameter type
rules.summary: Arguments passed to collection methods taking Object, like remove or contains, must match the collection's element type, or the operation silently fails.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling remove/contains with a value of a different type than the element type.
rules.compliant_concept: Pass arguments of the collection's parameterized element type.

exceptions.summary: Passing a differently typed object to a collection's equals() is acceptable.
Legacy code iterating mixed-type collections may pass mismatched types when the no-op outcome is intended.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Cannot know element types, so many correct calls look suspicious.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Implicit widening/boxing mismatches like short vs Short are missed.

rules.title: Do not follow a write by a subsequent write or read of the same object within an expression
rules.summary: Within one expression, avoid writing a variable and then writing or reading it again, since evaluation-order reasoning becomes error-prone.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Expressions like i = i++ + x or multiple assignments to the same variable.
rules.compliant_concept: Split side-effecting operations into separate statements.

exceptions.summary: Increment and decrement operators are allowed, unless the modified value is read or written again.
Writes followed by reads or writes are fine when in separate operands of || or &&.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Idiomatic patterns using short-circuit operators or simple increments may be flagged.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Writes via method calls or aliases within the expression are missed.

rules.title: Expressions used in assertions must not produce side effects
rules.summary: Assertion expressions must be free of side effects, since assertions may be disabled and the effect would then disappear.
rules.noncompliant_concept: assert containing assignment, increment, or a state-changing method call.
rules.compliant_concept: Compute side effects separately, then assert on the resulting value.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Pure method calls inside assert get flagged as possible side effects.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Side effects hidden in called methods are not evident.

rules.title: Prevent loss of useful data due to weak references
rules.summary: Data held only through weak references can be reclaimed unexpectedly; keep strong references to objects whose state must persist.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Configuring an object reachable only weakly, such as a logger, then losing its settings.
rules.compliant_concept: Hold a strong reference for as long as the configured state is needed.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags weak-reference caches that are designed to tolerate collection.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Weakly held objects not matching known APIs like Logger are missed.

rules.title: Do not operate on files in shared directories
rules.summary: Avoid file operations in directories that untrusted users can write, since links, races, and device files can redirect or subvert them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating or opening files in shared world-writable directories like /tmp without precautions.
rules.compliant_concept: Operate only within secure directories accessible solely by the owner.

exceptions.summary: Single-user systems or those without shared directories need not verify secure directories.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags shared-path usage on single-user systems or in tests.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Directory security depends on runtime paths and permissions not in source.

rules.title: Create files with appropriate access permissions
rules.summary: When creating files, set restrictive access permissions explicitly so that sensitive contents cannot be read or altered by other users.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating sensitive files with default or world-accessible permissions.
rules.compliant_concept: Specify restrictive permissions at creation, e.g. owner-only POSIX attributes.

exceptions.summary: Default permissions are acceptable for files created in secure directories unreadable by untrusted users.
Files lacking privileged content may use whatever permissions they are given by default.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags files containing non-sensitive data or created in already secure directories.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Insecure umask or permissions set by later calls or deployment are missed.

rules.title: Detect and handle file-related errors
rules.summary: Detect and handle errors from file operations, notably the boolean results of methods like delete, rename, and mkdir.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Ignoring the return value of File.delete or renameTo.
rules.compliant_concept: Check results and handle failure, or use Files methods that throw.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags ignored results where failure is truly inconsequential.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Errors swallowed through wrapper methods are invisible.

rules.title: Remove temporary files before termination
rules.summary: Temporary files must be removed before the program terminates, and created securely to avoid leaks and races.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating temp files that persist after use or rely solely on deleteOnExit.
rules.compliant_concept: Delete temp files explicitly after use, e.g. with DELETE_ON_CLOSE.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags temp files deleted in other methods or by cleanup frameworks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Missed deletions on exceptional paths are not identifiable syntactically.

rules.title: Release resources when they are no longer needed
rules.summary: Release system resources like streams, connections, and locks promptly after use, including on exception paths, rather than relying on garbage collection.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Opening a resource and not closing it on all paths.
rules.compliant_concept: Use try-with-resources or close in finally.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Resources closed by callers or ownership-transferring wrappers look leaked.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Leaks on exception paths and via fields or returned resources are missed.

rules.title: Do not expose buffers or their backing arrays methods to untrusted code
rules.summary: Do not hand untrusted code buffers that wrap internal arrays or their backing arrays, which permits modification of private state.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Returning ByteBuffer.wrap(internalArray) or a duplicate from a public method.
rules.compliant_concept: Return a read-only view or a copy of the buffer.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags buffers intended to be shared with trusted callers.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Exposure via fields or indirect returns is not traced.

rules.title: Do not create multiple buffered wrappers on a single byte or character stream
rules.summary: Do not wrap one underlying byte or character stream with more than one buffering wrapper, since each may consume data the other expects.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating multiple BufferedReader or Scanner instances over System.in or the same stream.
rules.compliant_concept: Create one buffered wrapper and share it.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags wrappers created at different times over separate streams of the same name.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Multiple wrappers created in different methods are not correlated.

rules.title: Do not let external processes block on IO buffers
rules.summary: When launching external processes, consume their output and error streams and supply needed input so they do not block on full buffers.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling waitFor or exitValue without draining process output streams.
rules.compliant_concept: Drain streams concurrently or redirect them via ProcessBuilder.

exceptions.summary: Process streams guaranteed to be unused by the subprocess may be ignored.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags processes whose streams are redirected elsewhere or that produce no output.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Stream handling done in separate helpers is not recognized.

rules.title: Distinguish between characters or bytes read from a stream and -1
rules.summary: Store results of InputStream.read and Reader.read in an int and test for -1 before narrowing to byte or char, so end-of-stream is distinguishable.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Casting read() result to byte or char before comparing to -1.
rules.compliant_concept: Keep the int result, compare with -1, then cast.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags casts after an earlier correct -1 check.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Narrowing via intermediate variables or helpers is missed.

rules.title: Do not rely on the write() method to output integers outside the range 0 to 255
rules.summary: OutputStream.write(int) emits only the low eight bits; do not use it to write values outside 0-255 expecting them preserved.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing an int that may exceed byte range with write(int).
rules.compliant_concept: Range-check values or use DataOutputStream.writeInt for full integers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags writes of values that are already constrained to byte range.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Value ranges computed elsewhere are not tracked.

rules.title: Ensure the array is filled when using read() to fill an array
rules.summary: A single read into an array may fill it only partly; check the returned count and loop or use readFully to obtain all required bytes.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling read(byte[]) once and assuming the buffer is full.
rules.compliant_concept: Loop until all bytes are read or use DataInputStream.readFully.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags reads where partial results are correctly handled later.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Read counts used incorrectly despite being stored are missed.

rules.title: Do not convert between strings and bytes without specifying a valid character encoding
rules.summary: Deprecated rule (moved): conversions between strings and bytes should name an explicit valid character encoding rather than using the platform default.
rules.noncompliant_concept: new String(bytes) or getBytes() with no charset argument.
rules.compliant_concept: Pass an explicit Charset such as StandardCharsets.UTF_8.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags default-charset conversions in contexts where encoding is irrelevant (ASCII-only).
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Readers/writers or third-party APIs that implicitly use the default charset are missed.

rules.title: Provide methods to read and write little-endian data
rules.summary: When exchanging binary data with little-endian systems, provide explicit byte-order handling, because DataInput/DataOutput methods assume big-endian.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Reading little-endian data with DataInputStream.readInt and similar big-endian methods.
rules.compliant_concept: Use ByteBuffer with explicit ByteOrder or byte-reversing helpers.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags big-endian methods used with data that is genuinely big-endian.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: The external byte order is unknowable from code alone.

rules.title: Do not log sensitive information outside a trust boundary
rules.summary: Sensitive data such as credentials, personal identifiers, or secrets must not be written to logs that are accessible outside the trust boundary.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Logging passwords, tokens, or personal data at any log level.
rules.compliant_concept: Omit or mask sensitive values before logging.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Variable-name heuristics flag non-sensitive values with suggestive names.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sensitive values with innocuous names or reached through objects are missed.

rules.title: Perform proper cleanup at program termination
rules.summary: On termination, perform necessary cleanup such as flushing and closing resources; be aware that halt and abnormal exits skip shutdown hooks.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling Runtime.halt or exiting without closing or flushing outputs.
rules.compliant_concept: Close resources before exit and use shutdown hooks for cleanup.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags exits where no unflushed state exists.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.summary: XML parsers processing untrusted documents must be configured to reject or safely resolve external entities and DTDs.

rules.summary: Native methods should be private and reached only through Java wrapper methods that perform validation, security checks, and defensive copying.

rules.summary: Native code must not assume Java strings are null-terminated; use lengths provided by JNI string functions (under construction).

false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.title: Use private final lock objects to synchronize classes that may interact with untrusted code
rules.summary: Classes reachable by untrusted code should synchronize on private final lock objects rather than this or class objects, preventing hostile lock acquisition.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Synchronized methods or synchronized(this) in a public class exposed to untrusted callers.
rules.compliant_concept: Synchronize on a private final Object lock not visible outside the class.

exceptions.summary: A documented class not handed to untrusted code, with a documented sync policy, may skip private locks.
A subclass may support client-side locking on its class object if its superclass documents doing so.
Package-private classes hidden from untrusted callers are exempt; document reliance on this.

false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.title: Do not synchronize on objects that may be reused
rules.summary: Do not synchronize on objects that may be shared or reused, such as boxed primitives, interned strings, or Boolean constants.
rules.noncompliant_concept: synchronized on an Integer, Boolean, or String literal or interned value.
rules.compliant_concept: Synchronize on a dedicated private final Object.

rules.summary: Do not synchronize on getClass(), which may return a subclass object; lock on an explicit class literal or private lock.

rules.compliant_concept: synchronized on Foo.class or a private static lock.

false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.summary: Do not use the intrinsic monitor of high-level concurrency objects like Lock or Condition; use their own locking methods instead.

rules.compliant_concept: Synchronize on the synchronized backing collection object.

false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.

rules.summary: Static fields that untrusted code can modify must have their access properly synchronized.

rules.compliant_concept: Guard access with a private static lock or use atomic types.

rules.summary: Avoid client-side locking on objects of classes that do not document their locking policy; use composition with private locks.

false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Transitive reflection paths are missed.

rules.title: Enable serialization compatibility during class evolution
rules.summary: Serializable classes should keep serialized form compatible across class evolution, e.g. by declaring an explicit serialVersionUID or serialPersistentFields.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Serializable class without explicit serialVersionUID that evolves.
rules.compliant_concept: Declare serialVersionUID and manage serialized form changes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags Serializable classes that are never persisted or exchanged across versions.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Incompatible field changes made despite a stable serialVersionUID go unnoticed.

rules.title: Do not deviate from the proper signatures of serialization methods
rules.summary: Serialization hook methods like readObject, writeObject, readResolve, and writeReplace must match the exact required signatures, or the runtime silently ignores them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: readObject or writeObject declared public, non-void, or with wrong parameters.
rules.compliant_concept: Private hook methods with the precise signatures the serialization mechanism expects.
false_positive_risks: Methods with hook names and stream parameters in classes that are not Serializable are reported.
false_negative_risks: Private readResolve/writeReplace in extensible classes and misspelled hook names are not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: Non-private, static, or non-void writeObject/readObject/readObjectNoData and static readResolve/writeReplace.

rules.title: Sign then seal objects before sending them outside a trust boundary
rules.summary: Objects crossing a trust boundary should be signed and then sealed, giving integrity and confidentiality in the correct order.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Sealing before signing, or transmitting serialized objects without signing and encryption.
rules.compliant_concept: Wrap in SignedObject first, then encrypt with SealedObject.

exceptions.summary: Signing an already-sealed object is reasonable to certify the sealed object's authenticity itself.
Objects staying entirely within a trust boundary require no signing or sealing.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags objects that never leave the trust boundary.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether data crosses a trust boundary is not visible in code patterns.

rules.title: Do not serialize unencrypted sensitive data
rules.summary: Sensitive data must not be serialized in cleartext; exclude it from the serialized form or encrypt it.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Serializable class holding passwords, keys, or personal data in non-transient fields.
rules.compliant_concept: Mark sensitive fields transient, use custom serialization, or encrypt them.

exceptions.summary: Sensitive data may be serialized once it has been properly encrypted.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Name-based sensitivity heuristics flag harmless fields.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sensitive data with neutral field names or nested objects is missed.

rules.title: Do not allow serialization and deserialization to bypass the security manager
rules.summary: Serialization and deserialization paths must apply the same security manager checks that guard ordinary construction and mutation.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Custom readObject or writeObject that skips permission checks enforced by setters or constructors.
rules.compliant_concept: Repeat the relevant security checks inside the serialization methods.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags classes whose state has no security-sensitive checks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Missing checks cannot be inferred without knowing which checks other paths perform.

rules.title: Do not serialize instances of inner classes
rules.summary: Instances of non-static inner classes should not be serialized, because their serialized form depends on compiler-generated fields.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A non-static inner or local class that implements Serializable.
rules.compliant_concept: Use static nested classes or make the inner class non-serializable.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags inner classes that are Serializable by inheritance but never serialized.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Serializable inherited from supertypes in other files is not detected.

rules.title: Make defensive copies of private mutable components during deserialization
rules.summary: readObject must defensively copy private mutable components so attackers cannot keep references into the deserialized object's internals.
rules.noncompliant_concept: readObject keeping deserialized mutable fields like Date or arrays without copying.
rules.compliant_concept: Clone or copy mutable fields in readObject before validation and storage.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags fields whose types are actually immutable.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mutability of field types is unknown without type resolution.

rules.title: Do not use the default serialized form for classes with implementation-defined invariants
rules.summary: Classes with invariants specific to their implementation should define a custom serialized form rather than rely on default serialization.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Default serialization of singletons or classes whose fields must satisfy invariants.
rules.compliant_concept: Custom readObject/writeObject, transient fields, or readResolve that enforce invariants.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags classes without meaningful invariants.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Invariants are implicit and not detectable syntactically.

rules.title: Minimize privileges before deserializing from a privileged context
rules.summary: Before deserializing within a privileged context, reduce privileges so attacker-controlled objects cannot exploit elevated permissions.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling readObject inside doPrivileged with full permissions.
rules.compliant_concept: Deserialize under a restricted access control context with minimal permissions.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags privileged deserialization of fully trusted data.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Privileged context established by distant callers is not visible.

rules.title: Do not invoke overridable methods from the readObject() method
rules.summary: readObject must not invoke methods that subclasses can override, since they run before the object is fully restored.
rules.noncompliant_concept: readObject calling a non-final, non-private instance method.
rules.compliant_concept: Call only private or final methods from readObject.

exceptions.summary: readObject() may call ObjectInputStream's overridable defaultReadObject() and readFields().

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags calls to ObjectInputStream methods like defaultReadObject that are permitted.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Overridable calls reached through helper methods are missed.

rules.title: Avoid memory and resource leaks during serialization
rules.summary: Serialization should not leak memory or resources, e.g. by streams retaining references to every written object indefinitely.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Long-lived ObjectOutputStream writing many objects without reset.
rules.compliant_concept: Periodically call reset() and bound the lifetime of serialization streams.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags short-lived streams that are closed promptly.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Stream reuse spanning methods or fields is missed.

rules.title: Prevent overwriting of externalizable objects
rules.summary: Externalizable classes must prevent readExternal from being invoked on an already initialized object to overwrite its state.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Public readExternal that unconditionally overwrites fields of an existing instance.
rules.compliant_concept: Track initialization and reject repeated readExternal calls.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags classes whose guard is implemented in a helper.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Guards that exist but are bypassable are not evaluated.

rules.title: Prevent deserialization of untrusted data
rules.summary: Untrusted data must not be deserialized unless the classes it may instantiate are restricted, e.g. by look-ahead allowlisting.
rules.noncompliant_concept: ObjectInputStream.readObject on network or user-supplied bytes without class filtering.
rules.compliant_concept: Override resolveClass or use serialization filters with a strict allowlist.

exceptions.summary: Serialized data from a documented trusted source may be deserialized without sanitization.

false_positive_risks: Streams protected by a JVM-wide serial filter or by a filter installed in a helper are reported.
SER12-EX0 trusted sources are reported for review.
false_negative_risks: Deserialization through streams created in other methods, XMLDecoder, or third-party serializers is not detected.

implementation.coverage_note: readObject/readUnshared on a same-method ObjectInputStream without an installed filter or look-ahead subclass.

rules.title: Don't form strings containing partial characters from variable-width encodings
rules.summary: Strings must not be built from byte sequences that split a multibyte character, since decoding partial characters corrupts data.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Decoding each fixed-size byte chunk of a variable-width encoded stream into a separate String.
rules.compliant_concept: Accumulate all bytes before decoding, or decode via a Reader that handles character boundaries.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags chunked decoding where the encoding is single-byte or chunks align with character boundaries.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Chunk boundaries arising from reads in other methods or loops are not recognized.

rules.title: Do not assume that a Java char fully represents a Unicode code point
rules.summary: A single char cannot represent every Unicode code point; supplementary characters span surrogate pairs and need code-point-aware handling.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Iterating or classifying text one char at a time, e.g. Character.isLetter(char), ignoring surrogates.
rules.compliant_concept: Use codePointAt, Character methods taking int code points, and advance by charCount.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags char loops over data guaranteed to be within the Basic Multilingual Plane.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Char-based logic hidden in helper methods or substring arithmetic is missed.

rules.title: Specify an appropriate locale when comparing locale-dependent data
rules.summary: Locale-sensitive operations such as case conversion, comparison, and formatting must use an explicit appropriate locale rather than the default.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling toUpperCase()/toLowerCase() or date formatting without a Locale for identifiers or protocol data.
rules.compliant_concept: Pass an explicit Locale (e.g. Locale.ROOT) or use locale-independent comparisons.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags default-locale conversions intended for user-facing display text.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Other locale-dependent APIs, like Formatter or Scanner, may not be in the pattern list.

rules.title: Do not encode noncharacter data as a string
rules.summary: Binary data that is not character text must not be converted into a String, since arbitrary byte patterns may not round-trip through a charset.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Creating a String from raw binary bytes, such as BigInteger or ciphertext bytes, for storage or transport.
rules.compliant_concept: Keep binary data as bytes, or encode it with Base64 or an equivalent textual encoding.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags new String(bytes) where the bytes genuinely contain encoded text.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Binary origin of byte arrays produced in other methods is not tracked.

rules.title: Use compatible character encodings when communicating string data between JVMs
rules.summary: String data exchanged between JVMs as bytes must use compatible, explicitly specified character encodings on both ends.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Writing and reading inter-process bytes using each JVM's default charset.
rules.compliant_concept: Specify the same named charset explicitly on both the producer and consumer.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags default-charset conversions for purely local, non-exchanged data.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Mismatched explicit charsets across separate programs cannot be correlated.

rules.title: Do not invoke Thread.run()
rules.summary: Calling a Thread's run() method directly executes it in the current thread; use start() to begin a new thread.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Invoking run() on a Thread object rather than start().
rules.compliant_concept: Call start() so the task runs in a newly created thread.

exceptions.summary: Unit tests may invoke run() directly, though this does not test multithreaded behavior.
Runtime system code that starts threads may call a Thread's run() method directly.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags run() on plain Runnables or within unit tests where direct invocation is fine.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Thread-typed receivers declared elsewhere or via subclasses go unrecognized.

rules.title: Do not invoke ThreadGroup methods
rules.summary: Avoid ThreadGroup methods; the class is obsolete, its operations are not thread-safe, and executors offer safer thread management.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using ThreadGroup methods such as activeCount, enumerate, or interrupt to manage threads.
rules.compliant_concept: Manage threads with executor services and explicit task tracking.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags harmless ThreadGroup accessors such as getName.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: ThreadGroup obtained through getThreadGroup chains or variables may not match.

rules.title: Notify all waiting threads rather than a single thread
rules.summary: Wake waiting threads with notifyAll/signalAll unless every waiter awaits the identical condition and only one may proceed.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Using notify() or signal() when waiters wait on different conditions.
rules.compliant_concept: Use notifyAll()/signalAll() or distinct Condition objects per predicate.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags notify() where a single homogeneous waiter set makes it safe.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Whether waiters share a condition requires semantic reasoning about predicates.

rules.title: Always invoke wait() and await() methods inside a loop
rules.summary: wait() and Condition.await() must be called in a loop that rechecks the condition, guarding against spurious wakeups and stolen notifications.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling wait() or await() under an if statement or unconditionally.
rules.compliant_concept: Place wait()/await() inside a while loop testing the condition predicate.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags waits looped by an enclosing method's caller.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Waits invoked through wrapper methods or on non-obvious receivers are missed.

rules.title: Ensure that threads performing blocking operations can be terminated
rules.summary: Threads that block on I/O or similar operations must have a reliable way to be stopped, such as closing the resource or using interruptible channels.
rules.noncompliant_concept: A thread blocked on socket reads with no mechanism to interrupt or close it.
rules.compliant_concept: Close the underlying resource, use interruptible channels, or cancel statements.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags blocking calls in threads that are short-lived or have timeouts.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Termination mechanisms implemented elsewhere are not linked to the blocking call.

rules.title: Do not use Thread.stop() to terminate threads
rules.summary: Never stop threads with Thread.stop(), which releases monitors abruptly and can leave objects inconsistent.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Calling Thread.stop() to terminate another thread.
rules.compliant_concept: Use interruption or a volatile flag checked by the thread.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags stop() on unrelated types that share the method name.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Calls via reflection or wrappers are missed.

rules.title: Use thread pools to enable graceful degradation of service during traffic bursts
rules.summary: Use bounded thread pools instead of creating a thread per request, so traffic bursts degrade service gracefully rather than exhausting resources.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Spawning a new Thread for each incoming request or task.
rules.compliant_concept: Submit tasks to a bounded executor service.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags thread creation for long-lived workers that is not per-request.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Unbounded executors like cached thread pools look compliant syntactically.

rules.title: Do not execute interdependent tasks in a bounded thread pool
rules.summary: Do not run interdependent tasks in a bounded thread pool, where tasks waiting for each other can exhaust the pool and deadlock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Pool tasks submitting subtasks to the same bounded pool and blocking on their results.
rules.compliant_concept: Avoid interdependence, use separate pools, or use caller-runs/fork-join.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags nested submissions to unbounded or separate pools.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Dependencies via shared queues or latches across classes are missed.

rules.title: Ensure that tasks submitted to a thread pool are interruptible
rules.summary: Tasks submitted to thread pools must respond to interruption so pools can shut down or cancel them.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Tasks that block indefinitely without checking interrupt status.
rules.compliant_concept: Make tasks interruptible by honoring interrupts and using interruptible operations.

exceptions.summary: Short, non-blocking tasks are exempt from this rule.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags short non-blocking tasks exempt from the rule.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Blocking calls inside helper methods are missed.

rules.title: Ensure that tasks executing in a thread pool do not fail silently
rules.summary: Tasks executing in thread pools must report abnormal termination instead of failing silently.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Runnable submitted via submit() whose exceptions are never retrieved or logged.
rules.compliant_concept: Use afterExecute hooks, uncaught exception handlers, or check Future results.

exceptions.summary: Allowed only when all tasks are audited to show exceptional conditions cannot occur.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags tasks whose Futures are inspected elsewhere.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Exception handling configured at pool construction is not linked to submissions.

rules.title: Ensure ThreadLocal variables are reinitialized when using thread pools
rules.summary: ThreadLocal values must be reinitialized for each task when threads are reused by pools, preventing state leakage between tasks.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Setting ThreadLocal state in pool tasks without clearing it afterward.
rules.compliant_concept: Reset ThreadLocal in finally blocks or in beforeExecute hooks.

exceptions.summary: ThreadLocal values that never change after initialization need not be reinitialized.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags ThreadLocals that hold immutable per-thread state.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: ThreadLocal usage spread across classes is not traced.

rules.title: Do not override thread-safe methods with methods that are not thread-safe
rules.summary: Subclasses must not override thread-safe methods with implementations that are unsafe for concurrent use.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Overriding a synchronized method with an unsynchronized one.
rules.compliant_concept: Preserve the superclass's synchronization policy in overrides.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags overrides that are thread-safe by other means.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Thread-safety of superclass methods not marked synchronized is unknown.

rules.title: Do not let the this reference escape during object construction
rules.summary: The this reference must not escape during construction, as other threads may see a partially constructed object.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Registering listeners or publishing this from a constructor.
rules.compliant_concept: Publish after construction completes, e.g. via factory methods.

exceptions.summary: A constructor may create a thread so long as it is started only after construction finishes.
Using the ObjectPreserver pattern is considered safe and is permitted.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags creating but not starting threads in constructors, which is permitted.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Escape via inner classes or helper calls is missed.

rules.title: Do not use background threads during class initialization
rules.summary: Class initialization must not start background threads that depend on the class being initialized, which risks deadlock.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Static initializer starting a thread that accesses the class's statics and joining it.
rules.compliant_concept: Initialize statics directly or defer thread use until after class initialization.

exceptions.summary: Background threads may start during class initialization if they cannot access any fields.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags background threads that access no class fields.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Threads started indirectly from static initializers are missed.

rules.title: Do not publish partially initialized objects
rules.summary: Objects must not be published to other threads before they are fully initialized.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Assigning a new object to a non-volatile shared field before construction completes.
rules.compliant_concept: Use final fields, volatile, synchronization, or safe publication idioms.

exceptions.summary: Partially initialized objects may be published if the class blocks their use until initialization completes.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags publication of immutable objects with final fields.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Publication via collections or indirect references is missed.

rules.title: Ensure visibility when accessing shared primitive variables
rules.summary: Shared primitive variables accessed by multiple threads need visibility guarantees through volatile, atomics, or synchronization.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Thread flags read in loops without volatile or synchronization.
rules.compliant_concept: Declare shared variables volatile or use atomic classes or locks.

exceptions.summary: Class objects need no extra visibility handling; the JVM initializes them before any use.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags fields only used by a single thread.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Which fields are shared between threads is unknown syntactically.

rules.title: Ensure visibility of shared references to immutable objects
rules.summary: References to shared immutable objects must be published with visibility guarantees.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Updating a non-volatile shared reference to a new immutable object.
rules.compliant_concept: Make the reference volatile or use synchronization or AtomicReference.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags references confined to one thread.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sharing across threads is not visible.

rules.title: Ensure that compound operations on shared variables are atomic
rules.summary: Compound operations like increments or check-then-act on shared variables must be atomic.
rules.noncompliant_concept: count++ on a shared field without synchronization, even if volatile.
rules.compliant_concept: Use synchronized blocks or atomic classes.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags compound operations on thread-confined variables.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Compound operations split across statements or methods are missed.

rules.title: Do not assume that a group of calls to independently atomic methods is atomic
rules.summary: A sequence of individually atomic method calls is not atomic overall; group them under a lock or use atomic composite operations.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Check-then-act on a synchronized or concurrent collection without external locking.
rules.compliant_concept: Use putIfAbsent-style methods or synchronize around the sequence.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags sequences where atomicity is not required.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sequences spread across methods are missed.

rules.title: Ensure that calls to chained methods are atomic
rules.summary: Chained method calls on shared objects, like builder sequences, must be performed atomically when accessed concurrently.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Multiple threads invoking chained setters on a shared builder.
rules.compliant_concept: Use thread-confined builders or synchronize the chain.
false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags chained calls on thread-local objects.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sharing of the receiver is not visible.

rules.title: Ensure atomicity when reading and writing 64-bit values
rules.summary: Reads and writes of shared 64-bit long and double values must be atomic, using volatile or synchronization.
rules.noncompliant_concept: Unsynchronized access to shared non-volatile long or double fields.
rules.compliant_concept: Declare such fields volatile or guard all accesses.

exceptions.summary: 64-bit long/double accesses are atomic if all reads and writes occur within synchronized regions.
Platforms guaranteeing atomic 64-bit long/double access may ignore this rule, sacrificing portability.

false_positive_risks: If implemented as a syntax-only rule: Flags fields on platforms with atomic 64-bit access or only accessed under locks.
false_negative_risks: This rule pack contains no detection for this rule; an absence of findings is not evidence of compliance.
Syntax-only detection limit: Sharing across threads is not visible syntactically.
